newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods buys UKCL scratchcards, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods buys UKCL scratchcards, sees growth.

text.p: The leisure arm of privately-owned British retail and gambling group Littlewoods said on Monday it had acquired a so-called scratch-card lottery ticket company, UK Charity Lotteries, for an undisclosed sum.

Littlewoods already has a product in the scratchcard market, which is otherwise dominated by the National Lottery products of the Camelot consortium, and said the acquisition of UKCL and its "Lucky" branded cards would give a combined annual group turnover in the developing market of 70 million stg.

"The acquisition of UKCL is an important step that confirms Littlewoods' commitment to the UK scratchcard market. The market is in its infancy and I am confident that in the long term (it) will develop as it has in more mature overseas markets," the managing director of Littlewoods Leisure, Colin Thwaite, said in a statement.

Littlewoods and UKCL will form a combined group, operating from headquarters in London, that expects to have over 40,000 outlets and should represent "a serious alternative to Camelot", the company said.
Littlewoods Leisure includes both the fast-growth lottery business and the company's traditional football pools business.

Since the launch of the national lottery in 1994, Littlewoods said, the British market for what it calls "soft gaming" has risen in value to 5.0 billion stg from 500 million, and it added that it saw potential for further growth "especially in the instant lottery market".
